statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Overnight Nasdaq-100 conditions are orderly and low-amplitude ahead of the US August employment report at 12:30 UTC.
recommendation: Assessment favours a narrow evidence-based danger window around the payrolls release rather than a broad session-wide restriction; Tail remains below the block threshold on current evidence.
headline: Quiet overnight drift near the range high with the August payrolls report the session's defining checkpoint
body: NQ futures trade near 29,639, about +0.39%, inside a narrow overnight range of roughly 29,482 to 29,639, after the Nasdaq-100 cash index closed Sep 3 at 29,482.32, up 1.16%, with a day range of 29,160.96 to 29,538.76. The Sep 3 session was broadly risk-on: the Nasdaq Composite rose about 1.4% and the Dow added roughly 635 points, its best day since Aug 4, after Fed Governor Christopher Waller signalled openness to a September hold, which cut September hike odds from 63.2% to 50.4% on CME FedWatch and pushed the 10-year yield down about 5 basis points to roughly 4.75%. VIX closed at 14.32, down 5.79%. The H.15 release for Sep 2 shows the 2-year at 4.39% and the 10-year at 4.79%. Cross-asset conditions are not aligned in a way that denies mean reversion: WTI near $91.53 is up roughly 10% on the week on renewed Strait of Hormuz supply risk, yet that strength has not transmitted into sustained index downside. Megacap and semiconductor dispersion is wide, with Tesla up 5.4% and Broadcom down 2.7% despite an earnings beat, which argues for mixed rather than one-way structure. The overnight drift holds the upper part of its range but spans only about 157 points, so it is shallow rather than persistently directional. The August Employment Situation at 12:30 UTC, with consensus near +58K payrolls against a prior -23K and an unemployment rate consensus of 4.1%, is the defining checkpoint; event proximity is scored primarily into Stress and Confidence rather than into the assessed pathological price-path risk.

lookbackSummary: The past 24 hours are fully covered by published Claude assessments. Conditions were benign through the European session on Sep 3 with Tail near 13 and the mode assessed as normal, shifted to trend-up with Tail peaking at 21 across the US cash session as the Waller-driven rally developed, then decayed back through the evening. Overnight into Sep 4 the mode returned to normal with Tail between 12 and 14 and Stress easing to the low 50s.
outlookSummary: The baseline path holds a low-amplitude range through the Asian and European sessions, with Stress building into the 12:30 UTC August employment report. The release hour carries the widest two-sided repricing risk of the window and is modelled at Tail 23, which maps to WATCH rather than a block, consistent with the framework treating event importance as a Stress and Confidence input until persistent one-way structure is actually observed. Tail is modelled decaying through the US afternoon as the release is absorbed, with a small uptick into the Friday power hour on long-weekend position squaring ahead of the Labor Day holiday on Sep 7. CME equity index futures halt for the weekend at 21:00 UTC, so the final eight slots carry a closed-market floor with reduced Confidence reflecting the absence of a live price path. The main invalidation of this outlook would be observed post-release continuation with shallow or failed retracements, particularly through the 13:30 UTC cash open.
